summary: Sudden spike in 5xx errors after liveness-probe burst triggered runtime eviction loop
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-14T09:12 UTC we observed a rapid increase in 5xx responses originating at the API gateway for tenant Acme Analytics. Symptoms included: 502/503 spikes for short-lived streaming connections, elevated streaming disconnects, and a correlated increase in runtime pod evictions and GPU reinitialization events. Impact: Customer-facing real-time embeddings and chat inference experienced timeouts and disconnects for ~18 minutes, impacting dashboards and alerts for Acme (dedicated capacity). Scope: Single region (us-east) affected; multiple model variants for the tenant saw increased error-rate. Initial mitigation removed the tenant from the high-priority route, which reduced error amplification but did not fully resolve underlying evictions.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate sustained liveness-probe flapping by issuing rapid healthcheck failures to ephemeral proxies (repeat 5s interval for 2 minutes).
Ramp a small stream fanout from the tenant to the dedicated pool (concurrent streams ~120 per GPU node).
Observe API gateway logs for 502/503 and runtime for eviction messages and NVML/GPU reinit traces.
observed_behavior: API gateway returned a spike of 502/503 for streaming endpoints with request latencies spiking then abrupt runtime pod evictions. Runtime logs show repeated 'evicting worker due to liveness failure' and subsequent GPU driver reinitialization messages. Upstream proxies reported conn reset and accept queue backlog growth.
expected_behavior: Stable streaming with graceful handling of liveness probe flakiness: gateways should queue/hedge without causing eviction cascade and runtime should avoid full worker eviction for transient probe failures.
logs: 2026-03-14T09:12:22Z apigw-us-east-1 ERROR accept queue depth=512 -> 5xx surge
2026-03-14T09:12:26Z runtime-node-17 WARN evicting worker id=342 reason=liveness-failure count=1
2026-03-14T09:12:29Z runtime-node-17 ERROR nvml: driver reinit after device reset
2026-03-14T09:28:05Z apigw-us-east-1 INFO route failover applied for tenant=acme-analytics
investigation_notes: 09:14 UTC - SRE: Noticed liveness probe failures on ephemeral proxies coincident with an automated health check sweep from a new internal canary job. Slack: #incidents links: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01INCIDENT/xyz
09:16 UTC - Support: Removed tenant from priority route to reduce fanout; 5xx rate decreased from 8% -> 2% but runtime evictions continued for ~6 minutes.
09:18 UTC - Eng: Correlated NVML resets to eviction events; kernel logs show repeated GPU warmup failures after worker restart attempts.

Hypothesis A: Healthcheck sweep caused ephemeral proxies to briefly fail liveness checks which triggered scheduler to evict workers aggressively; eviction caused GPU reinitialization which increased latencies and further healthcheck failures (feedback loop).
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler/pod lifecycle settings are tuned too aggressively for liveness probe flakiness (short grace period + immediate eviction).
Heap/profile: no OOMs observed; CPU spike correlated with reconnect storms on proxy threads.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-14T09:20: Please confirm whether there's an external canary or job that started around 09:12 UTC - we see a matching healthcheck signature.
Priya Shah (SRE) 2026-03-14T09:23: Confirmed: internal canary job 'canary-liveness-sweep' ran a 2-min aggressive sweep in us-east at 09:11 UTC (investigating why it targeted ephemeral proxies).

Tomas Rivera (Eng) 2026-03-14T09:40: Initial mitigation: applied temporary policy to increase liveness grace for ephemeral proxies to 30s and paused the canary job. Monitoring for 30m to ensure no reoccurrence.
Acme-Analytics (Customer) 2026-03-14T09:45: They reported client-side retries saw 'socket hang up' errors and asked for ETA; we provided status updates and mitigation steps.
resolution: Mitigation implemented 2026-03-14T09:35: paused internal canary job and increased ephemeral-proxy liveness grace window from 5s -> 30s for us-east. This stopped the eviction cascade and reduced 5xx to baseline within ~4 minutes.

Root cause (preliminary): overly aggressive internal liveness sweep combined with tight eviction thresholds in the scheduler. The canary's target list included ephemeral proxies due to a config drift.

Permanent actions planned:
- Rework canary job scope to exclude ephemeral proxies and add rate limits on healthcheck sweeps.
- Adjust scheduler eviction policy to require N consecutive liveness failures before eviction (PR: runtime#9310).
- Add guard in autoscaler to avoid concurrent scale operations during healthcheck sweeps.
- Run a post-incident test to validate fix (owner: Tomas Rivera, due: 2026-03-20).
